intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is caused by mutation in the WASHC4 gene (KIAA1033; 615748) on chromosome 12q23.3.

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is caused by mutation in the WASHC4 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We conclude that KIAA1033 is responsible for a heterogeneous ARID phenotype, and additional description will be needed to refine the clinical phenotype.
checks.explanation: The paper reports compound heterozygous KIAA1033/WASHC4 variants as the cause of autosomal recessive intellectual disability. The MRT43 label is OMIM's name for the disorder and only restates this link.

checks.claim: The WASHC4 gene is also known as KIAA1033.
checks.evidence_quote: In 2011, KIAA1033/WASHC4 was associated with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The paper writes the gene as KIAA1033/WASHC4, so it treats the two names as the same gene.

checks.claim: The WASHC4 gene is located on chromosome 12q23.3.
checks.evidence_quote: a non-synonymous sequence change in the SWIP [Strumpellin and WASH (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein and scar homolog)-interacting protein] gene
checks.explanation: The chromosomal location is standard nomenclature added to the gene the paper identifies.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is a nonsyndromic form of intellectual disability (Ropers et al., 2011). It is caused by loss of function of SWIP (WASHC4) (Courtland et al., 2021). SWIP is a member of the WASH complex, which is involved in actin polymerization and endosomal transport (Ropers et al., 2011). The WASH complex activates Arp2/3-dependent actin branching at the outer surface of endosomes (Courtland et al., 2021).

checks.claim: Autosomal recessive intellectual developmental disorder-43 (MRT43) is a nonsyndromic form of intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Identification of a novel candidate gene for non-syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability: the WASH complex member SWIP.
checks.explanation: The title describes the disorder as non-syndromic autosomal recessive intellectual disability.

checks.claim: MRT43 is caused by loss of function of SWIP (WASHC4).
checks.evidence_quote: the data presented here support a mechanistic model whereby SWIPP1019R causes a loss of WASH complex function, resulting in endo-lysosomal disruption and accumulation of neurodegenerative markers
checks.explanation: The paper frames loss of WASH complex function as a mechanistic model driving the disorder, but does not use the name MRT43 and presents loss of function largely through the mouse model.

checks.claim: SWIP (WASHC4) is a member of the WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: the WASH complex member SWIP
checks.explanation: The paper states that SWIP is a member of the WASH complex.

checks.claim: The WASH complex is involved in actin polymerization and endosomal transport.
checks.evidence_quote: a member of the recently discovered WASH complex, which is involved in actin polymerization and multiple endosomal transport processes
checks.explanation: The paper states the WASH complex's roles directly.

checks.claim: The WASH complex activates Arp2/3-dependent actin branching at the outer surface of endosomes.
checks.evidence_quote: activating Arp2/3-dependent actin branching at the outer surface of endosomes to influence cargo sorting and vesicular scission
checks.explanation: The introduction states the WASH complex activates Arp2/3-dependent actin branching at the outer surface of endosomes.

paragraphs.text: Ropers et al. (2011) reported a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) reported a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive nonsyndromic intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID), we have combined homozygosity mapping
checks.explanation: The family is described in the abstract, and the title specifies the disability is non-syndromic.

paragraphs.text: The transmission pattern of MRT43 in the family reported by Ropers et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: The transmission pattern of MRT43 in the family reported by Ropers et al. (2011) was consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID)
checks.explanation: The paper describes the disorder in this family as autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability, Ropers et al. (2011) used homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment, and high-throughput sequencing to identify a mutation in the gene encoding SWIP (WASHC4). The mutation led to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex. Ropers et al. (2011) concluded that their findings suggested that SWIP is a novel gene for autosomal recessive intellectual disability.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) studied a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID), we have combined homozygosity mapping
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) used homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment, and high-throughput sequencing to identify a mutation in the SWIP (WASHC4) gene in a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: we have combined homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment and high-throughput sequencing to identify the underlying gene defect
checks.explanation: The methods and the identification of a SWIP change are both stated.

checks.claim: The SWIP (WASHC4) mutation identified by Ropers et al. (2011) led to significantly reduced SWIP levels.
checks.evidence_quote: we could show that this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The SWIP (WASHC4) mutation identified by Ropers et al. (2011) led to destabilization of the entire WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) concluded that their findings suggested that SWIP (WASHC4) is a novel gene for autosomal recessive intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Thus, our findings suggest that SWIP is a novel gene for ARID.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Courtland et al. (2021) made knockin mice carrying the Swip mutation that corresponds to the human pro1019-to-arg (P1019R) mutation. The mutant mice had less WASH complex. Their neurons showed endolysosomal abnormalities, and the mice developed cognitive and motor deficits.

checks.claim: Courtland et al. (2021) made knockin mice carrying the Swip mutation corresponding to the human P1019R (pro1019-to-arg) mutation in SWIP (WASHC4).
checks.evidence_quote: we generate a mouse model of the human WASHC4c.3056C>G mutation. Quantitative spatial proteomics analysis of SWIPP1019R mouse brain
checks.explanation: CRISPR knock-in of the P1019R mutation into murine Washc4 is described.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice had less WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: Western blot analysis of brain lysate from adult homozygous SWIPP1019R mutant mice (referred to from here on as MUT mice) displayed significantly decreased abundance of two WASH complex members, Strumpellin and WASH1
checks.explanation: Mutant mice showed decreased WASH complex components, i.e. less WASH complex.

checks.claim: Neurons of Swip P1019R knockin mice showed endolysosomal abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: Cellular and histological analyses confirm that SWIPP1019R results in endo-lysosomal disruption and uncover indicators of neurodegeneration.
checks.explanation: Mutant neurons showed endo-lysosomal structural abnormalities.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice developed cognitive deficits.
checks.evidence_quote: MUT mice showed a significant decrease in conditioned freezing to tone presentation compared to their WT littermates
checks.explanation: Cued fear memory deficit indicates cognitive impairment.

checks.claim: Swip P1019R knockin mice developed motor deficits.
checks.evidence_quote: also causes significant progressive motor deficits in mice
checks.explanation: The paper reports progressive motor deficits in the mutant mice.

paragraphs.text: Ropers et al. (2011) found that the SWIP (WASHC4) mutation identified in a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (MRT43) led to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex.

checks.claim: Ropers et al. (2011) identified a SWIP (WASHC4) mutation in a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (MRT43).
checks.evidence_quote: In a large consanguineous family with autosomal recessive intellectual disability (ARID), we have combined homozygosity mapping, targeted exon enrichment and high-throughput sequencing to identify the underlying gene defect.
checks.explanation: A SWIP mutation was identified in this family. The MRT43 label is standard OMIM nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SWIP (WASHC4) mutation identified by Ropers et al. (2011) in a family with MRT43 led to significantly reduced SWIP levels.
checks.evidence_quote: we could show that this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: The SWIP (WASHC4) mutation identified by Ropers et al. (2011) in a family with MRT43 led to destabilization of the entire WASH complex.
checks.evidence_quote: this mutation leads to significantly reduced SWIP levels and to destabilization of the entire WASH complex
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Courtland et al. (2021) introduced the mutation corresponding to the human pro1019-to-arg (P1019R) mutation into mice and found that it caused a loss of WASH complex function.

checks.claim: Courtland et al. (2021) introduced into mice the Swip mutation corresponding to the human WASHC4 P1019R (pro1019-to-arg) mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: we were able to introduce the same point mutation in exon 29 of murine Washc4 using CRISPR
checks.explanation: This mutation is the human WASHC4 c.3056C>G / P1019R mutation introduced into mice.

checks.claim: Courtland et al. (2021) found that the mouse Swip mutation corresponding to human WASHC4 P1019R caused a loss of WASH complex function.
checks.evidence_quote: SWIPP1019R causes a loss of WASH complex function, resulting in endo-lysosomal disruption
checks.explanation: The paper concludes the mutation causes loss of WASH complex function.
